title: Understand the AWS Shared Responsibility Model

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud security is shared between AWS and the customer. Shared does not mean every task is divided equally; responsibility follows the layer each party controls.
bullets: Components of the AWS shared responsibility model
How the boundary changes with Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and AWS Lambda
sections.callout: Who controls and must secure this layer?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: Service choice → Moves the responsibility boundary
sections.callout: AWS = OF · CUSTOMER = IN · SERVICE = MOVES THE LINE

sections.title: AWS Shared Responsibility Model
paragraphs: The model divides cloud security and management responsibilities between AWS and the customer because each controls different parts of the environment.
bullets: Some responsibilities belong primarily to AWS
Some belong primarily to the customer
Some require participation from both sides
The exact division depends on the service
sections.callout: AWS + CUSTOMER = SHARED RESPONSIBILITY—not a literal 50/50 split.

sections.title: AWS Responsibility — Security OF the Cloud
paragraphs: AWS protects the infrastructure that runs AWS Cloud services.
bullets: Underlying infrastructure that delivers AWS services

sections.title: Customer Responsibility — Security IN the Cloud
paragraphs: Customers secure the parts of the environment they control. The exact list changes by service.
bullets: Guest operating system responsibilities on applicable services
sections.callout: You control it → you must secure it.

sections.title: Shared Responsibilities
paragraphs: AWS handles its part of the technology and operational controls, while the customer handles the corresponding responsibilities within the resources and configurations the customer controls.
sections.callout: AWS securing its infrastructure does not correct a customer's unsafe data, identity, code, or configuration decisions.

sections.title: The Responsibility Boundary Moves by Service
paragraphs: The more managed the service, the more of the underlying stack AWS operates. Customer data, access, permissions, and customer-controlled configuration remain important throughout the ladder.
sections.callout: EC2 → RDS → Lambda: AWS progressively manages more underneath.

sections.title: Amazon EC2
paragraphs: AWS operates the physical infrastructure beneath the virtual machine. The customer controls and secures much more of the guest environment.
sections.callout: EC2 guest OS patching → Customer responsibility

sections.title: Amazon RDS
paragraphs: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service. Compared with installing a database on EC2, AWS manages more of the database platform and underlying environment.
bullets: AWS manages more of the underlying database platform
Customer remains responsible for customer-controlled configuration
sections.callout: Managed service does not mean zero customer security responsibility.

sections.title: AWS Lambda
paragraphs: AWS Lambda runs code without the customer managing servers directly. AWS operates the underlying infrastructure and runtime environment, while the customer remains responsible for secure code, data, permissions, access, and configuration.
sections.callout: Bring the code; AWS manages much more underneath.

table.caption: Responsibility shifts as AWS manages more of the service

entries.title: Security OF vs. IN the Cloud
paragraphs: AWS secures the cloud infrastructure. The customer secures what the customer controls in the cloud.

entries.title: Physical Infrastructure vs. Customer Configuration
paragraphs: AWS facilities and hardware → AWS. Customer resource configuration → Customer.

entries.title: EC2 Guest OS vs. Physical Host
paragraphs: Guest OS on EC2 → Customer. Physical infrastructure under EC2 → AWS.

entries.title: RDS vs. EC2
paragraphs: Database installed on EC2 → Customer manages more. Amazon RDS → AWS manages more of the database platform.

entries.title: Lambda vs. EC2
paragraphs: EC2 leaves more of the computing environment to the customer. Lambda shifts more underlying management to AWS.

entries.title: Managed Service Trap
paragraphs: Managed does not transfer responsibility for customer data, access, code, permissions, or customer-controlled configuration to AWS.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Shared cloud security → AWS shared responsibility model
Physical data center and hardware → AWS
Managed database platform → RDS / AWS manages more
Serverless underlying infrastructure → Lambda / AWS manages more
Different service changes the boundary → Responsibility shifts by service
